title: Components and vertical DVR stalks of a regular proper flat trait scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $g:T\to S$ be proper and flat [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism], with $T$ Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian) and regular [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Assume $T_k$ is reduced [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme], every local ring of $T$ has dimension at most two, and the local ring in $T$ at every closed point of $T_k$ has dimension two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $T$ is a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed integral regular schemes $T_i$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], each meeting both $T_K$ and $T_k$, and each of topological Krull dimension two [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $T_k$, viewed as a point of $T$, the local ring $A=\mathcal O_{T,\xi}$ is a DVR whose maximal ideal is generated by the nonzero image of $\pi$; moreover $A/\pi A$ is the residue field of that generic point [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-residue-field]. The empty scheme is allowed, giving an empty disjoint union; otherwise every $T_i$ is nonempty. No nodality, connectedness, projectivity, excellence, completeness or residue-field perfection is assumed.

source.place: Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian) and Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension); algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), condition (4). Proper-flat trait specialization and reduced-special-fibre application expanded from the terminal steps of lem-sfb-nodal-trait-regularization.

proof.text: Apply [rem-pc-regular-normal](1),(2) to the regular Noetherian scheme $T$. Its irreducible components are finitely many pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subsets, each integral with its open subscheme structure; denote the nonempty ones by $T_i$. The local rings of an open subscheme equal the ambient local rings, directly from restriction of the structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. Hence each $T_i$ is regular. This already gives the asserted finite disjoint union, including the empty union if $T$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 033M, lemma-normal-Noetherian; regularity of open subschemes from Definition 02IS

proof.text: Fix a nonempty component $T_i$. It has a generic point $\eta_i$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Its local ring is a field by the integral clause of [lem-sc-rational-functions-generic-stalks]; the open immersion identifies this with $\mathcal O_{T,\eta_i}$. If $g(\eta_i)$ were the closed point of $S$, flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] would make multiplication by the nonzero $\pi\in R$ injective on this nonzero field. But the stalk homomorphism is local, so sends $\pi\in\mathfrak m_R$ into the zero maximal ideal of that field, a contradiction. A DVR has just the primes $(0)$ and $(\pi)$: in a local principal ideal domain every nonzero prime is maximal. Thus $g(\eta_i)$ is the generic point and $T_i$ meets $T_K$, using the underlying-space description of [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, integral clause; flat local stalk argument

proof.text: Because $T_i$ is closed in $T$ and $g$ is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], $g(T_i)$ is closed in $S$. It contains the generic point by Step 2, so equals $S$. Thus choose $x\in T_i\cap T_k$. The space of $T$ is quasi-compact ($T$ is Noetherian) and Kolmogorov: for $y\ne z$ the closures $\overline{\{y\}},\overline{\{z\}}$ are irreducible closed with generic points $y,z$, so by uniqueness in [lem-sc-scheme-sober] they differ and the complement of one of them is an open set containing exactly one of $y,z$. Applying [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] to the nonempty closed subset $\overline{\{x\}}$ of $T$ gives a specialization $c$ of $x$ that is closed in $T$. The subsets $T_i$ and $g^{-1}(s)$ are closed, so $c$ lies in both, and is closed in $T_k$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The hypothesis gives $\dim\mathcal O_{T,c}=2$. Open restriction identifies this with $\mathcal O_{T_i,c}$, while every local ring of $T_i$ has dimension at most two. The equality of topological dimension with the supremum of local-ring dimensions [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] now gives $\dim T_i=2$.

source.place: topology.tex Tag 005E, topology-lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point; properties.tex Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension; properness Definition 01W1 in morphisms.tex

proof.text: Let $\xi$ be a generic point of an irreducible component $Z$ of the reduced scheme $T_k$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $T_k$ containing $\xi$. Then $Z\cap U$ is an irreducible component of $U$: it is irreducible closed in $U$, and any larger irreducible closed subset has irreducible closure in $T_k$ containing $Z$, contradicting maximality. Consequently the prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $\xi$ is minimal by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. The ring $B$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The affine stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] give $\mathcal O_{T_k,\xi}\cong B_{\mathfrak p}$, a field. It therefore equals its residue field by [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible (3); Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring; affine stalk identification in schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6)

proof.text: Set $A=\mathcal O_{T,\xi}$. It is a Noetherian local ring by regularity [def-weil-regular-scheme], and a domain by Step 1 and the meaning of normality in [rem-pc-regular-normal]. Since $g(\xi)=s$, flatness and [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] make multiplication by $\pi$ injective on $A$; as $1\ne0$, its image $t$ in $A$ is nonzero. Apply [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] at $\xi$ and use $\mathfrak m_R=(\pi)$ to obtain $A/tA\cong\mathcal O_{T_k,\xi}$. By Step 4 this is a field, so $tA$ is maximal and must be the unique maximal ideal of $A$. Now [lem-sc-principal-ideal-dvr] makes $A$ a DVR with maximal ideal $(t)$. The displayed quotient, followed by the residue-field identification of Step 4, is precisely $A/\pi A\cong\kappa(\xi)$ as asserted.

The statement is true. Small cases: the empty scheme; P^1_R, whose vertical stalk is R[x]_(pi); Spec R and Spec K, which fail the hypotheses; P^1 over a ramified R' with non-reduced special fibre, which is excluded; and a reducible reduced special fibre. The only statement change, def-weil-geometric-fibre -> def-pc-scheme-fibre for T_k, corrects the citation and weakens a hypothesis, so the item gets stronger. Its only citer, nodal-trait-regularization step 4, gets geometric reducedness from nodality, and that implies the ordinary fibre is reduced. All five steps check: (1) regular => normal => finite clopen integral components (033M); (2) a vertical component is impossible, since a flat field stalk is torsion-free over R but the local map sends pi to 0; (3) the image of T_i is closed and contains the generic point, so T_i meets T_k; a point closed in T and in T_k has local dimension 2, and 04MU gives dim T_i = 2; (4) a component of T_k meets an affine open in a component, given by a minimal prime of a reduced ring, so the stalk is a field; (5) A is a Noetherian local domain, t != 0 by flatness, A/tA = fibre stalk (0HA1) is a field, so m_A = (t) and 00PD(4) makes A a DVR.
